Counsel for Appellant :- S.K. Mehrotra Counsel for Respondent :- Vidya Kant Shukla Hon'ble Vipin Chandra Dixit,J.
1) Heard Sri S.K. Mehrotra, learned counsel for the appellants and Sri Vidhya Kant Shukla, learned counsel for claimants-respondent Nos. 1 to 4.
No one is present for respondent no.5.

2) This first appeal from order has been filed by the appellant against the judgment and award dated 15.4.2014 passed by Additional District Judge/Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Court No.12,
Kanpur Nagar in M.A.C.P. No.845 of 2010 (Smt. Manjusha Shukla and others vs. Manish Kumar Tripathi and another), by which compensation of Rs.4,84,460/- alongwith 6% interest has been awarded in favour of claimants on account of death of Shashi Kant Shukla.

sentences.text: 3) It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that involvement of insured vehicle in the accident is seriously doubtful.
The Claimants have failed to prove the involvement as well as rash and negligent driving of the driver of the vehicle which was insured with the appellant.

The accident H.D.F.C. Ergo General Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. Manjusha Shukla And 4 Ors. on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79858707/
1 was allegedly occurred on 20.10.2009 whereas the FIR of the said accident was lodged after more than 6 months on 2.5.2010.

entities.text: H.D.F.C. Ergo General Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. Manjusha Shukla And 4 Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the claimants, in collusion with owner of the vehicle, have planted the insured vehicle with the intention to get compensation.
It is further submitted that vehicle no. UP 72 E 1122 was mentioned in the FIR, whereas number of insured vehicle is UP 77 E 1112.
The Claims Tribunal has also erred in awarding Rs.1,14,960/- towards medical expenses which has not been proved by the claimants.

4) On the other hand, learned counsel appearing on behalf of claimants submits that claimants had fully proved involvement of Bolero jeep in the accident as well as rash and negligent driving of driver of the Bolero jeep by adducing cogent evidence.
The deceased had received grievous injuries in the accident.
He was hospitalized for more than one month.

The FIR was not registered by the police,
then claimant no.1 had filed an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. and FIR was registered after the direction of learned Judicial Magistrate and there is no deliberate delay on the part of claimants in lodging FIR.
It is further submitted that the Investigating Officer, after due investigation, has submitted charge sheet against the driver of Bolero jeep.

The claimants had also produced Jitendra Kumar Mishra as P.W.-2 who was an eyewitness of the accident and has proved the involvement of insured vehicle as well as rash and negligent driving of driver.
No evidence has been adduced by the opposite parties in rebuttal and even driver of Bolero jeep was not produced by the opposite parties before the Claims Tribunal.
5) So far as quantum of compensation is concerned, the claimants have filed cross appeal for enhancement of compensation.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the claimants-respondents that the claimants have proved the income of the deceased as Rs,6000/- per month but the Claims Tribunal has accepted notional income of Rs.3000/- per month.
The Claims Tribunal has also erred in not awarding any amount towards future prospects and only Rs.9500/- has been awarded for non-pecuniary damages.
It is further submitted that as per claim petition the age of the deceased was 38 years.

As per statement of P.W.-1, who is widow of deceased and postmortem report also, the age of the deceased was 38 years and the Claims Tribunal has erred in accepting the age of deceased in between 40-45 years.

6) Considered the rival submissions of learned counsels for the parties and perused the record.
7) As per case of the claimants, Bolero jeep No. UP 77 E 1112 had hit the motorcycle from behind.
The FIR was not registered by the concerned police station and as such, claimants had approached the concerned Court for registering the FIR by filing application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.
The FIR was lodged after direction of learned Judicial Magistrate.
The Investigating Officer, after due investigation, has submitted charge sheet against the driver of insured vehicle.

8) The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Ravi versus Badrinarayan & Ors. reported in AIR 2011 Supreme Court 1226 has held that the delay in lodging the first information report would not be fatal and claim petition under the Motor Vehicle Act need not be dismissed on that ground.

sentences.text: It is well-settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.

In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so;
the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
21. The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquility of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if, there is delay, the same deserves to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons."

9) A Division Bench of this Court in the case of Smt. Sumitra Kaur and another vs. New India Assurance Company Ltd. through Divisional Manager and another reported in 2012 (4) T.A.C. 799 (All.) has held that registration of first information report is not necessary to decide the claim petition filed under the Motor Vehicles Act, if the claimants have proved the involvement of vehicle as well as rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by producing cogent evidence.

entities.text: Smt. Sumitra Kaur and another vs. New India Assurance Company Ltd. through Divisional Manager and another reported in 2012 (4) T.A.C. 799 (All.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claims tribunal may decide the claim petition on merits and non-registration of first information report will not defeat the case of the claimants.
Relevant paragraphs 7 and 8 are reproduced hereinbelow:

"7. Power conferred to Tribunal under Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act is an independent power whereby the Tribunal has been required to hold an inquiry with regard to accident and award of compensation.
This should be done after providing opportunity of hearing to both parties.
Even where no first information report is lodged the Tribunal has ample power to hold an inquiry and admit or reject the claim petition keeping in view the evidence on record.
8. Under U.P. Motor Vehicle Rules, 1998 it has been provided that how the Tribunal shall record evidence and deal with the case.

Lodging the first information report or H.D.F.C. Ergo General Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. Manjusha Shukla And 4 Ors. on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79858707/
3 inquest report is not necessary.

entities.text: H.D.F.C. Ergo General Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. Manjusha Shukla And 4 Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: What is required for the Tribunal is that it must ascertain the involvement of the victim in the accident and genuineness of claim.

In case the Tribunal is satisfied from the evidence on record that accident occurred and the victim suffered injuries then even if no first information report has been lodged and postmortem is made available it may award the compensation."
10) In view of above, claimants have fully proved involvement of Bolero jeep in the accident as well as rash and negligent driving of driver of the Bolero jeep.
No ground for interference is made out.
The appeal filed by the Insurance Company is devoid of merits and is dismissed accordingly.
11) Interim order, if any, stands discharged.
12) The Claims Tribunal while calculating the compensation accepted Rs.3,000/- per month as income of the deceased.
The Claims Tribunal has recorded the finding that the claimants had failed to prove the income of the deceased as Rs.6000/- per month.
The finding recorded by Claims Tribunal is based on materials, which are available on record and there is no illegality in any manner.
The age of the deceased was established as 38 years.

The claimants-respondents are also entitled for 40% future prospects and Rs.70,000/- for non-pecuniary damages in view of law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi reported in 2017(4) T.A.C. 673.

sentences.text: So far as medical expense is concerned, claimants had filed bills and vouchers of Rs.1,14,960/- and there was no dispute about genuineness of bills and vouchers.
The Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded Rs.1,14,960/- towards medical expenses.
13) Cross appeal No.317524 of 2014 filed by claimants is liable to be allowed.

The compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is reassessed as under:-
1) Monthly income = Rs.3,000/-
2) Annual income = Rs. 3,000/- X 12 + Rs.36,000/-
3) Future prospects (40%) = Rs.14,400/-
4) Total annual income = Rs.36,000/- + Rs.14,400/- =Rs.50,400/-
5) Deduction towards personal expenses(1/3rd) = Rs.50,400/- - Rs.16,800/-
=Rs.33,600/-
6) Multiplier applicable (15) =Rs.33600/- x 15 = Rs.5,04,000/-
7) Non-pecuniary damages =Rs.70,000/-
8) Medical Expenses = Rs.1,14,960/-
Total = Rs.5,04,000/- + Rs.70,000/- + Rs.1,14,960/- = Rs.6,88,960/-

sentences.text: 4 14) In view of aforesaid discussion, the Cross Appeal No.317524 of 2014 filed by claimants is hereby allowed and award of the Claims Tribunal is modified and compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.4,84,460/- to Rs.6,88,960/-.
The claimants-appellants are also entitled for 6% interest on enhanced amount from the date of judgement and award of Claims Tribunal dated 15.4.2014.
15) The HDFC General Insurance Company Limited-appellant is directed to pay enhanced amount alongwith interest to the claimants-appellants within two months from today.
16) The statutory deposit of Rs.25,000/- shall be remitted to the claims Tribunal for adjustment to the amount deposited by the appellant.
